title: Safety after simulator initialization
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$, and let $x$ be any input word over the folded alphabet. Starting the folding simulator on $x$ and taking one step yields a configuration satisfying the safety invariant: its state is not the fresh initial state, all work-head positions are nonnegative, and every nonnegative work-tape cell has its origin flag set exactly at position $0$.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$
$x$ is any word over the folded alphabet
replaced:
Let $M$ be a multi-tape machine over a finite alphabet with decidable equality.
For every input over the folded alphabet --- including inputs containing symbols
outside the range of the alphabet embedding --- the configuration reached after one
step of the folding simulator from its initial configuration satisfies the safety
invariant.
